notes.headline: This mix is clipping hard at +2.8 dBTP and squashed to -2.7 LUFS — pull the mix bus limiting off and rebounce with headroom before anything else.
notes.summary: The balance side of this mix is in good shape: left/right sit dead even, correlation is healthy, and mono fold-down barely costs you anything. The problem is the output stage. You're bouncing at -2.7 LUFS with true peaks at +2.8 dBTP and only 5.5 dB of peak-to-loudness, which means something on the Stereo Out is doing heavy limiting. For a mix going to mastering that's all cost and no benefit — it distorts on playback and lossy encoding, and it removes the transient range a mastering engineer needs. Fix the output chain and this bounce scores a 10.

priorities.title: Take the limiting off the mix bus and rebounce with headroom
priorities.why: True peak at +2.8 dBTP is above full scale, so you're already hearing distortion that will get worse after MP3/AAC encoding. At -2.7 LUFS Spotify turns you down about 11.3 dB anyway, so the loudness buys nothing, and a 5.5 dB peak-to-loudness ratio means drum transients are being flattened before mastering ever sees them. These three readings are the same problem: a limiter doing work that doesn't belong at the mix stage.

priorities.title: Rebuild section contrast once the limiter is off
priorities.why: Loudness range is 3.5 LU, which is very little movement between sections. Some of that will return on its own when the limiter comes off; whatever's left is worth drawing in by hand so verses and choruses read as different.

listen_for: Solo the drum bus after the limiter is bypassed — kick and snare transients should have attack again rather than a flat front edge.
Check the loudest section on headphones or anything with a converter that shows clipping; the crunch you may have been reading as saturation should be gone once peaks land in the −6 to −3 dBFS range.
Play the verse into the chorus back to back at a fixed monitor level and confirm the lift is audible without reaching for the fader.
Flip to mono briefly to confirm the low end still holds together after the gain change — it measured fine, so you're checking nothing broke.
strengths: Left/right balance is 0.0 dB — nothing is pulling to one side.
Mono fold-down only costs 0.56 dB, so the mix translates to mono playback cleanly.
Low-end correlation at 0.785 means your bass is centered and phase-coherent.

judge.priority_order: The critical true-peak/loudness/PLR cluster (F1,F2,F3) is placed first and the info-level LRA issue (F4) second, matching severity ordering.
judge.explains_impact: Priority 1 explains distortion on playback/encoding and flattened transients before mastering, and priority 2 explains sections failing to read as different, not just citing numbers.
judge.groups_causes: F1, F2 and F3 are correctly merged as one limiter-caused issue while F4 (section contrast) is kept separate as its own cause.
judge.specific: Notes cite the exact measurements (+2.8 dBTP, -2.7 LUFS, 5.5 dB PLR, 3.5 LU, 0.785 low-end correlation) rather than generic advice.
judge.stage_appropriate: Notes treat the mix as heading to mastering, criticizing loudness only insofar as it signals unwanted limiting/headroom loss rather than judging it against streaming loudness targets.
judge.faithful: All claims (distortion risk, Spotify turn-down, transient flattening, mono/LR strengths) trace directly to the report's measurements and findings without contradiction.
judge.concise: Each section stays tied to a specific measurement or action with minimal repetition, and the listen_for/strengths lists are short and purposeful rather than padded.
